I have farmed this land in Quzhou for 50 years. My 4.1 mu is all I have, and I know every corner of it. At my age, I do not try new tricks—I stick to what works. My winter wheat went into the ground last October after rotary tillage. Now that spring has arrived, I will irrigate three times: at green-up, at jointing, and at heading. I topdress with urea twice during the growing season. I use an improved wheat variety from the local seed station that has given me stable yields around 500 kg per mu. For pests, I spray herbicide once in early spring, and if I see aphids or rust, I add insecticide and fungicide—about three sprayings in total.

After I harvest the wheat in early June, I plant hybrid maize the same day or the next. There is no time to waste in the summer season, so I seed directly into the wheat stubble with no deep tillage. Hybrid seed is the only choice for maize these days. I put down compound fertilizer at sowing and topdress with nitrogen when the maize reaches the big-flare stage. I irrigate twice in summer if the rain does not come in July and August. One herbicide spray and one insecticide spray are enough for maize if you time them right. I expect about 600 kg per mu from the maize if the autumn rains hold. My household has three mouths to feed, and this plan has kept us secure for decades.
